rules.title: Xcode older than 15 is not accepted for App Store uploads
rules.summary: Apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 15 for iOS 17, iPadOS 17, tvOS 17, or watchOS 10 starting April 29, 2024.

constraints: Keep .xcode-version, CI Xcode selections, and local installs on one Xcode release that App Store Connect still accepts.
Later App Store SDK minimums also require newer Xcode lines; plan to land on the current minimum (see the replacement).

steps.title: Raise the Xcode pin
steps.instructions: Change the reported .xcode-version (or equivalent CI Xcode version) from the rejected line to a release App Store Connect accepts (see the replacement).

steps.title: Align other Xcode surfaces
steps.instructions: Update CI macOS/Xcode images and documented install steps so they match the new pin.

verification.purpose: Confirm the active Xcode is the intended release.
Build with the new Xcode before uploading to App Store Connect.
Build and test the Swift package on the toolchain that matches the new Xcode.

rules.title: Xcode 15 through 25 are not accepted for App Store uploads
rules.summary: Since April 28, 2026. Apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using an SDK for iOS 26, iPadOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, or watchOS 26.

sources.title: SDK minimum requirements — App Store upcoming requirements (Xcode 26)

constraints: Keep .xcode-version, CI Xcode selections, and local installs on one Xcode release that App Store Connect still accepts.

steps.title: Raise the Xcode pin
steps.instructions: Change the reported .xcode-version (or equivalent CI Xcode version) from the 15–25 line to Xcode 26 or later.

steps.title: Align other Xcode surfaces
steps.instructions: Update CI macOS/Xcode images and documented install steps so they match the new pin.

verification.purpose: Confirm the active Xcode is the intended release.
Build with the new Xcode before uploading to App Store Connect.
Build and test the Swift package on the toolchain that matches the new Xcode.

rules.title: iOS and iPadOS app targets below iOS 13 are not accepted for App Store uploads
rules.summary: Since September 9, 2026, iOS and iPadOS apps uploaded to App Store Connect must target iOS 13 or later.

sources.title: iOS and iPadOS minimum system requirements — App Store upcoming requirements

constraints: Set the deployment target on the app target that is uploaded, not on a library or Swift package: libraries that declare an older platforms minimum are not changed by this rule.
Raising the minimum removes iOS releases from the app's audience, and can remove APIs the app relies on; keep the minimum your users still run at or above 13.

steps.title: Raise the iOS deployment target
steps.instructions: Set IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET on each build configuration of the app target to 13.0 or later (see the replacement), and keep it consistent across Debug and Release.

steps.title: Align other deployment surfaces
steps.instructions: Update the minimum version in documentation, release notes, and any App Store Connect or TestFlight metadata that names the old minimum.

verification.purpose: Confirm the app target resolves to the raised deployment target.
Build the app for iOS with the raised deployment target before uploading.
